item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This one's a very strong -1 from me.

The writing is a bit slipshod, and could use some editing just to clean up portions so they're easier to read, in a general sense.

+ show block
– hide block

Over time, the ectoplasm making up individual manifestations will “evaporate” and rise back up to the main body of SCP-460. This may take anywhere from several days to a few weeks, depending on the temperature and general humidity of the area. Once SCP-460 starts moving again, any remaining manifestations are instantaneously vaporized, and the cycle starts over.

The concept itself is kind of vague and not well managed - why does this storm being stationary mean anything? Why do the ghosts disappear IMMEDIATELY when it starts moving? From the description, it makes more sense for them to stop when it stops raining, or when the ectoplasm evaporates. That said, why is the ectoplasm evaporating when it's still ecto-raining? While I personally don't have the rabid distaste for the use of ectoplasm as terminology, I do also agree that there's very little explanation around that either - no samples, no commentary about it, not even a 'There's this stuff that's making ghosts and the researchers are calling it ectoplasm'.

Addendum: Due to the outcome (or lack thereof) of Incident 460-b and 460-c, item has been reclassified as Euclid.

What are Incidents 460-b and 460-c? If you're never going to mention anything about them BESIDES the fact that these incidents exist, they mean literally nothing. This is especially egregious to me because those incidents are apparently connected to a reclassification AWAY FROM KETER. That's kind of a big deal.

Observation Log 460-a
All relevant reports from Mu-13 are to be catalogued and formatted as follows:

As with the previous addendum, all of this information is actually COMPLETELY meaningless. There is no context whatsoever. We get a location and some pisspoor descriptions of the circumstances, again plagued by the slipshod writing. I'd rather have just the dates than just the locations. Location means nothing - dates give a sense of how long the MTF has been dealing with this particular anomaly, give us the sense of how much of a problem this has been. Individual references at scattered locations across the globe do not. Why are these INDIVIDUAL(emphasis on singular events referenced at each location) ghosts more notable? And if this anomaly is making ENTIRE CITIES start raising ghosts…where are the rest of them?

item.content:encoded: This seems like the kind of thing that would be quickly publicized. There is no procedure for how to handle the information of these "Ghosts". Overall, it just fit into the SCP style in my opinion. I mean, ectoplasm? Come on. It seems lazy that you didn't go with the redacted or blacked out materials from other dimensions or those only known by the foundation.

No idea what Andariel's issue was with the dog being called Spot. It had a tag that said Spot, so they called it Spot… I don't understand the rant about Scott.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Glad I'm not the only one with rustled jimmies over the "ectoplasm" usage, or as we call it "the outer, non-granulated part of a cell's cytoplasm"

Also:
– hide block

Of note is that not only humans are capable of returning as a ghost, but also all sentient life that possesses a purpose for their manifestation.

So, only humans are capable of returning, unless this thing has been recorded headed out to sea. Or else we're using whatever subjective definition of "sentience" the author has determined on their own.

manifest in a physical form as ghosts

Considering that ghosts don't exist, this basically means nothing. Some zombies can run, some zombies can use weapons, some zombies shuffle about at a snail's pace, some zombies aren't even dead or undead, some zombies vomit blood, some zombies have tentacles, some zombies can swim.

Subject returned to former home, reconciled with husband and children.

At what point did the screaming and calling for exorcists cease?

I guess I'm just going to have to assume the definition of ghost here is "utterly indistinguishable from normal, except that they disappear eventually". Though unless the husband and children didn't know the mother had died, when did the screaming and calling up exorcists stop?

Subject attempted to apprehend a manifestation, which promptly revealed his true nature

Who's true nature? If the spooky ghosty's, where is it ever described that the manifestations have cloaks of disguise and actually look like memetic skeletons underneath that go "boo" at people hard enough to cause a heart attack, unless this police officer had serious heart conditions that somehow didn't interfere with his ability to be a police officer who chases down suspects.

No resemblance to subject before death, resembled a twisted, disturbing interpretation of a norse troll.

Again, a Norse troll does not exist, so this statement basically means nothing, even if you are familiar with Norse mythology (which I am not).

Speaking of meaning nothing overall, how in the shit was this ghosty identified if it looked (and behaved, since this was a serial killer, not a random mass murderer) absolutely nothing like its living self?

Dematerialized early, the first example of living beings able to influence manifested spirits on the physical plane.

Absolutely nothing in the paragraph written describes anything providing this "example". If it was communication, that was already established by the first one, so this is basically pointless or else misplaced chronologically.

Subject: Spot, formerly a domesticated canine.

Subject appeared to be a manifestation of a mixed breed dog of unverifiable heritage, wearing a small collar engraved with the name “Spot”

I don't even know how to begin questioning this line of insanity. "We found a headless, limbless torso with a nametag reading 'Scott' somewhere in the state of Georgia, so we've found our missing person Scott, the only person with this name in the entire state of Georgia, nevermind that the missing Scott was a fat black man and this torso is that of a skinny white man."

Subject followed Mu-13 during the entirety of the session. Dematerialized normally, to the dismay of Mu-13, which had grown fond of its company.

"Dismay"? Are these task force people even remotely trained? If they were so distressed about it, they could adopt their own fucking dogs, there's a huge supply of delightful doges available at any animal shelter.

Overall, this whole thing is an empty mess, even by "old standards"

Not bad at all! IMHO is's just asking for more experimental information, such as /e.g./:
- is there a correlation between the amount of ectoplasmatic precipitation and the number of ghosts? or other observables?
- what exactly seems to cause appearance of the long-dead?
- what are the physical and mental properties of the manifestations?
- what exactly triggers manifestation of an individual? Contact of ectoplasma with the remains? With the point of death? Something else?
- how would this work on dead sentient SCPs, especially ones who come back to life?

And many more.
